Omitting `settings.preset` is how you ask Lighthouse for mobile: its DEFAULT emulation is a mid-tier phone on a throttled 4G link with 4x CPU slowdown. Until now the site was only ever measured on the desktop preset, which applies no CPU throttling and a fast link — so nothing here had ever been checked on the device most visitors use. lighthouserc.spec.ts pins which assertions must match the desktop file and which are allowed to differ, so the LCP exception below cannot quietly spread.

//lcp-why-not-2500: 2500ms is unreachable on this architecture, and that is a measured claim rather than an opinion. LCP can never precede FCP, and mobile FCP is 2258-2686ms on every audited route: / 2258, /blocks 2686, /templates 2569, /compare 2414, /blocks/hero-split 2498. Two routes exceed 2500ms at FCP ALONE, so no amount of LCP-element tuning can pass a 2500 gate. The cause is structural — the site is fully client-rendered (`<div id=app>` ships empty), so nothing is contentful until the whole critical path lands and mounts Vue: 226.5 kB gzip (entry 135.5 + vendor-vue 37.1 + vendor-icons 17.0 + CSS 37.0). Evidence that it is the WHOLE path and not one trimmable chunk: cutting the entry by 19 kB gzip during this task moved FCP by approximately nothing. Getting under 2500 needs prerendered above-the-fold HTML (SSG) so first paint stops waiting on JS. That is the next lever and it is a much larger change than this task.
//lcp-ratchet: Measured 2026-07-20, Lighthouse 13.4.0 mobile emulation, medians of 3 interleaved runs per route across TWO independent sessions (two vite preview ports round-robined A,B,A,B — sequential before/after on a dev machine is drift, not signal). After, as a range across both sessions: / 2456-2528ms, /compare 2733-2739ms, /blocks 2939-3074ms, /templates 2953-3653ms, /blocks/hero-split 3559-3572ms. Before, same sessions: / 2658-2707, /compare 2879-2895, /blocks 2895-2896, /templates 3088-3402, /blocks/hero-split 4192-4296. The big win is /blocks/hero-split, -737ms and reproducible; /templates is the noisiest route and its spread is main-thread jitter, not a fixable resource (its LCP element is a text lede, TTFB 10ms + render delay 276ms — there is no LCP image to preload, which is why no image lever was applied).
//lcp-why-4000: 4000 has to satisfy two opposing constraints. Tight enough to BIND: the worst route measured 4192-4296ms locally before this work (4340ms in the 2026-07-16 CI note), so reverting it fails the gate — a ceiling above ~4300 would be decoration. Loose enough not to paint CI red on day one, which is what the previous note rightly refused to do: the worst measured median after this work is 3653ms, leaving ~350ms. CAVEAT, stated plainly: these are LOCAL numbers on a dev machine, and CI runners read higher — the historical CI note recorded /blocks at 4.15s where this machine measures 2.9s. So 4000 is PROVISIONAL and the first CI run on this gate is the real calibration. If CI lands well under it, tighten it. If CI cannot hold it, the correct response is to re-measure ON CI and set the ceiling from that evidence, recorded here with the run link — a one-time calibration, not a habit. After that first calibration the number may only ever move DOWN. Do not resolve a red gate by reverting to `warn`; that is how this metric went unwatched for four months.
